title: Compact staging slabs and single-shot memcpy scheduler to reduce host-GPU overhead
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
Multiple production traces show high host-side overhead during prefill→decode handoff. Symptoms: many small memcpy invocations from fragmented pinned buffers, frequent short-lived threadpool tasks creating contention, and repeated kernel-selection stalls while waiting for small transfers. These manifest as elevated p50/p95 host CPU consumption, noisy GC-like allocation patterns for pinned buffers, and periodic latency spikes under mixed workloads (short chat + long generation).

Hypothesis:
If we compact host staging into per-worker pinned slabs and schedule aggregated single-shot memcpy operations (grouping contiguous requests within a short window), we can reduce syscall/count overhead, reduce thread wakeups, and enable cleaner overlap between memcpy and kernel execution on the GPU. Combined with a small priority-aware transfer scheduler (short requests get expedited), we expect lower CPU usage, fewer context switches, and improved latency tail without materially increasing tail latency for large batches.

Proposed solution (implementation sketch):
1) Staging slabs: allocate one or two large pinned host slabs per CPU worker (configurable slab_size, e.g., 8MB). Replace ad-hoc pinned allocations with slab allocations and circular allocation pointers. Slabs are reclaimed by epoch to avoid fragmentation.
2) Aggregation window: introduce a short aggregation window (default 250–500us) that collects small prefill buffers destined for the same GPU/stream. Within the window, coalesce adjacent payloads into a single iovec-backed memcpy to the slab and then perform a single cudaMemcpyAsync (or equivalent) per slab flush.
3) Single-shot memcpy scheduler: a lightweight scheduler groups slab flushes and issues async transfers on a bounded number of transfer threads. Transfers use pinned staging and per-GPU DMA-capable streams, with completion callbacks that enqueue decode kernels.
4) Priority steering: requests tagged low-latency (short-chat) are eligible for higher priority and smaller aggregation windows (e.g., 100us) to keep p50 tight; long/bulk requests endure slightly larger windows to improve throughput.
5) Threadpool changes: reduce short-lived task creation by turning many small work units into a few composite tasks (slab-coalesce → single transfer → callback), reducing thread wakeups. Modify threadpool to support cooperative parking and per-worker affinity when slabs are in use.
6) Safety/backpressure: when slabs fill, fall back to existing behavior (split-off synchronous memcpy) and emit metrics. Add soft limits and a circuit-breaker to avoid unbounded memory.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Memory overhead: per-worker slabs increase total pinned memory. Mitigation: slab_size heuristics and per-pool caps; measure against memory-constrained Dedicated nodes.
- Increased scheduling complexity: aggregation windows introduce a small extra micro-latency; mitigated by priority steering and short defaults.
- Edge cases: highly skewed request sizes may lead to suboptimal coalescing. Add heuristics to bypass coalesce for single huge payloads.
- Platform differences: Windows or older kernels without io_uring optimizations might perform differently; implementation hides platform-specifics behind an abstraction layer.

Benchmarks (internal prototype):
- Setup: 8xA10 node, synthetic mixed workload (70% short-chat ~64 tokens, 30% long ~1024 tokens), baseline runtime-1.22.
- Prototype results (canary branch): p50 prefill→decode host time: 18.4ms -> 11.1ms (40% reduction); p95: 63ms -> 34ms (46% reduction); p99: 145ms -> 78ms (46% reduction).
- CPU: host user CPU cycles for prefill path down ~30% at 95th percentile; context switches down 55%.
- Memory: pinned memory increased by ~9% under the same qps.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flag gate: runtime flag "compact_staging_v1" default off for hosted; enable in Dedicated private clusters with opt-in config.
- Canary: enable for 10% of traffic in non-critical region (us-west-2) for 48h, monitor metrics (host_cpu_pre_fill_ms, transfer_count_per_request, context_switches, p50/p95/p99 latency).
- Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over multiple cycles with automated rollback if p99 or CPU exceed safe thresholds.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for slab allocation/free ordering, wraparound behavior, and failure paths.
- Integration tests with CUDA mocks to validate single-shot transfer completion ordering.
- Load tests using replay of production trace (one-hour window) to verify no regression in throughput and improved host metrics.
- Chaos test: simulate stalled transfers and slab exhaustion to ensure fallback path is correct.

Observability and metrics to add:
- transfer_aggregations_per_second (gauge), avg_payload_per_transfer (histogram), slab_fill_ratio (gauge), slab_alloc_failures (counter), transfer_latency_ms (histogram).
- Alerting on increased slab_alloc_failures or sustained transfer_latency_ms > baseline + 2x.

Docs and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3CompactStagingDesign
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8231
- Benchmark scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-scripts/tree/main/compact-staging

Acceptance criteria:
- p95 prefill→decode host time reduced by >= 30% on mixed workload replay for canary nodes.
- No increase > 10% in end-to-end p99 generation latency under production traffic shape.
- CPU host user cycles for prefill path reduced by >= 20% at 95th percentile.
- No regression in memory ops or observed OOMs in Dedicated nodes with configured slabs.

Next steps (short term):
- Complete threadpool affinity changes and integrate with slab allocator (Marco).
- Add metrics hooks and canary rollout automation (SRE/infra).
- Run full-production trace replay and capture a 24h diff.
- Prepare release notes and console observability tile for runtime-1.23.

Longer term ideas (future epics):
- Replace aggregation window with an adaptive latency estimator that dynamically tunes window per queue shape.
- Explore OS-level batching (io_uring) paths for non-CUDA DMA engines on supported kernels.
- Kernel-hinting integration so the kernel selector prefers models/variants that yield contiguous prefill layouts for even better coalescing.
